title: Marche Stays Below the National Average as a Week-Long Climb Continues
dek: Drivers in Marche are still paying less than the rest of Italy at the pump, even as both Benzina and Gasolio prices have risen for seven straight tracked days.
body: Self-service Benzina in Marche is averaging €2.056 per liter today, with Gasolio at €2.183 — both a step below the national self-service averages of €2.080 and €2.205. That gap, roughly 2.4 cents on Benzina and 2.3 cents on Gasolio, means a full 50-liter tank costs Marche drivers a bit over a euro less than the Italian average on either fuel.

The relief is only relative, though: Marche's prices have been climbing steadily, with self-service Benzina up nearly 2.7 cents and Gasolio up about 2.4 cents since September 3rd alone. Behind those numbers, the region's station network stayed essentially stable — 775 registered stations with 729 reporting prices today, versus 731 the day before, a normal day-to-day flicker rather than a sign of stations dropping out.

Tracking a single region this closely, every day, with same-day comparisons against the national picture, isn't something a manually updated spreadsheet could keep up with.
